results.title: Wall Type Issue, Especially in Maine | ResStock

item.text:
**Yes—ResStock documents a known, unresolved error in Maine’s Geometry Wall Type data.** Mislabeling in the underlying county tax assessor data produces implausible distributions: in 2024 Release 2, Maine’s single-family detached homes are approximately 10% wood frame, 12% brick, and 78% concrete block (CMU). The team believes **all published ResStock datasets are affected**, and no fix has been implemented. [Official issue report](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.html)

The ResStock team recommends:

- **For wall type or exterior finish distributions:** use nearby states as proxies, especially **Vermont and New Hampshire**.
- **For measures whose eligibility depends on wall type:** reweight Maine’s results using nearby states’ wall type distributions, or use nearby states’ measure results directly. Wood-frame-only insulation measures can otherwise appear applicable to too few Maine homes. [Recommended workaround](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.html)

The team currently does not expect significant effects on baseline energy consumption, emissions, or bills, or on those results where upgrades are applied, but the investigation remains incomplete. [Impact assessment](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.html)
